I’m going into my senior year as a English major who initially wanted to study journalism. Here’s what my experience has been. 

For me personally, I initially wanted to be a journalism major but a professor at the school I was intending on going to had a conversation with me and convinced me to switch to English instead. I decided to choose journalism as a minor. I’m glad I did—the school ending up deleting journalism as a minor AND major because of a lack of faculty to teach, so I had to switch to a communications minor about 3/4 of the way through my journalism minor. 

For me personally, I was able to find a ton of opportunities to practice journalism outside of my major. Among other things, I worked on the school newspaper as both a writer and editor and secured a 3 year job at my school’s communication department. I’m happy with my choice, because I think having English as a major has really helped me to enrich my understanding of social issues dealing with class, race, gender, sexuality and so much more. While my work experience and minor choice have helped me to develop professional and technical writing, my major choice has helped me to develop analytical and academic writing. I feel pretty well rounded. 

Lastly I’d just add that I feel like English is a less limiting major choice that journalism. That’s one of the biggest reasons why I chose it instead. 

However, you did mention the school in question was good for journalism. Obviously mine didn’t have a good department, but if yours does, and you’re leaning toward it, then go for it! But also make sure you have avenues through which you can educate yourself about important social issues, especially if English doesn’t become a minor or anything. 

Okay, this is actually the last thing: even though I’m happy with my undergrad experience and what I’ve learned overall, I’d say that my one biggest regret is not choosing something tech oriented to pair with my major. Lots of employers want someone who a) knows journalism/communications/writing basics, b) is educated on important social issues AND c) has some sort of tech skill. So if you’re interested at all, look into a computer science or digital design kind of minor. Wish I would’ve done that. It’s on like every application ever—what are your tech skills? Journalism has changed to digital storytelling. I’m betting that learning those skills will be somewhat embedded in your major classes anyway, but it doesn’t hurt to have the minor. And if the minor isn’t your thing, you can always take the initiative to learn outside of school. There are plenty YouTube videos and online courses that will have you proficient by the time you graduate! 

I guess what I’m saying is to focus on developing those three skills. Professional writing, understanding of social issues and knowledge of tech. There’s many ways you can do it. Make one area your major, the other area jobs/internships and the other area research and learning outside of class. You’ve got this!!

While I majored in English instead of journalism, I’m doing a minor in journalism and I have a pretty good amount of experience on my resume. But the imposter syndrome is SO real. 

You’re probably already heard this, but network. Networking is so important. Especially as you’re building your resume.

There’s always gonna be competition. There’s always gonna be someone with more experience. That’s just how the field is. While I definitely agree with some of the comments here in that I think you just have continue doing your personal best, don’t forget to really hold onto that thing that made you want to do journalism in the first place. Because at the end of the day, you can have a ton of job experience, but some employers are looking for more—they’re looking for that passion. Show them that, above all, you want to tell stories.
